sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Bladud is a figure of Welsh tradition, remembered as the fabled founder of the city of Bath. Some accounts name him as the father of the god Lludd. In the eighteenth century the commentator John Wood, writing in 1742, offered a fanciful proposal. He suggested that Bladud might be the same person as Abaris the Hyperborean. The story of Bladud ties the healing waters of Bath to a legendary royal founder. It gives the city a place in British mythical history.

okr.objective: Present Bladud as the Welsh fabled founder of the city of Bath.
